plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Hugh Huxley (1969, Science 164: 1356–1365), Lymn & Taylor (December 1971, Biochemistry 10: 4617–4624), and Ebashi (1963–1965, Nature) calcium-troponin switch & actomyosin cross-bridge cycle chart shows Ca2+ binding troponin to shift tropomyosin off actin binding sites, followed by ATP detachment from rigor, hydrolysis cocking, and Pi-release 10-nm power stroke.

teach_overlay.detail: Inked Hugh Huxley (1969, Science 164: 1356–1365), Lymn & Taylor (December 1971, Biochemistry 10: 4617–4624), and Ebashi (1963–1965, Nature) calcium-troponin switch & actomyosin cross-bridge cycle chart on period paper showing Ca2+ binding troponin to shift tropomyosin off actin binding sites, followed by ATP detachment, hydrolysis cocking, and Pi-release 10-nm power stroke
teach_overlay.scale: counterintuitively, a muscle doesn't need fresh ATP to grab the rope — it needs fresh ATP to let go of the rope for the next pull, which is why running out of ATP after death locks muscles rigid in rigor mortis
